# Natural Gas: Methane and Flaring {#sec-natural-gas-methane}

Methane released along the gas supply chain is the natural gas sector's largest controllable emission (see @sec-natural-gas). CIMS represents each source as its own node under the supply chain, with a competition among abatement options at each. Most of these nodes offer a **no abatement** option (pneumatic controls start instead from gas-driven devices), which leaves the methane vented or leaking as it does today at zero cost and energy, so the model buys down methane only where the carbon price or a regulation makes an abatement option cheaper.

Because the captured methane is saleable gas, many abatement options pay for themselves, which is why Canada's 75 % reduction target for 2030 is achievable at an average cost of only around $11–48 per tonne of CO₂-equivalent [@edf-methane-canada; @eccc-methane-og].

## Emission sources

| Source | What it covers | Measured in |
|:-------|:---------------|:------------|
| Well tests | Gas released during well testing and flowback after completion | t CH₄ |
| Venting: controls | Gas-driven pneumatic controllers and chemical-injection pumps | 1,000 m³ gas handled |
| Venting: blowdowns | Gas released when equipment and pipelines are depressurized for maintenance | t CH₄ |
| Venting: liquid unloading | Gas released when wells are blown down to clear liquids | t CH₄ |
| Venting: other point sources | Tank and process vents, and nitrogen rejection units | t CH₄ |
| Venting: other diffuse sources | Diffuse venting not otherwise classified (no technologies yet) | t CH₄ |
| Fugitive | Unintended leaks from equipment, compressors, and pipelines | t CH₄ |
| Flaring | Gas burned rather than vented or sold | t CO₂ |

: Methane and flaring sources in the natural gas supply chain {#tbl-natural-gas-methane-sources}

## Well tests

Reduced-emission completions capture the gas from a fractured well's flowback with portable separators instead of venting it.

{{< include _technology-blocks/natural-gas/product_supply_well-tests.md >}}

## Pneumatic controls

Gas-driven pneumatic devices vent methane by design. Low-bleed devices cut the vent rate; instrument air and electric actuators eliminate it.

{{< include _technology-blocks/natural-gas/product_supply_venting_controls.md >}}

## Fugitive leaks

Leak detection and repair finds and fixes leaking components; low-emission seals, valves, and connectors, and plastic liners in leak-prone distribution mains, cut the leak rate of the equipment itself.

{{< include _technology-blocks/natural-gas/product_supply_fugitive.md >}}

## Flaring

Flaring converts methane to CO₂, which is far less potent. Flare gas recovery sends the gas to the fuel or sales line instead, and high-efficiency flares cut the unburnt methane that escapes.

{{< include _technology-blocks/natural-gas/product_supply_flaring.md >}}
